title: A Scalable Algorithm for Active Learning
problem: FIRAL's active learning algorithm suffers from prohibitive complexity—O(c²d² + nc²d) storage and O(c³(nd² + bd³ + bn)) computation—making it impractical for large-scale datasets with many points n, dimensions d, and classes c.
motivation: Active learning reduces costly manual labeling, but FIRAL's computational bottlenecks prevent deployment on real-world large-scale datasets despite its strong theoretical guarantees.
method: The authors replace FIRAL's exact calculations with simpler approximations that reduce storage from O(c²d² + nc²d) to O(n(d+c) + cd²) and computation from O(c³(nd² + bd³ + bn)) to O(bncd²), while keeping the same prediction accuracy. To speed things up further, they implement this on GPUs working together in parallel. They then validate their approach using strong and weak scaling tests on large-scale vision datasets to show it scales well.
key_novelty: The core idea is to approximate FIRAL's calculations so it uses dramatically less memory and computation while maintaining prediction accuracy, enabling practical deployment across multi-GPU systems with million-point datasets.
contributions: Approximate algorithm reducing storage complexity by factors of c and d versus FIRAL
Computational complexity reduced to O(bncd²) from O(c³(nd² + bd³ + bn))
GPU parallel implementation validated on multiple datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10, Caltech101, ImageNet)
Empirical scaling validation up to 12 GPUs with no accuracy deterioration

metrics.speedup: Strong and weak scaling demonstrated on up to 12 GPUs
